symptom: `mxcli test`: an @expect written over two lines (` * @expect $r = 'a;b'` then ` *   and length($r) = 3`) kept only its first line with no message; --list, check and the run all asserted `$r = 'a;b'`, so with `and` the test passed on less than it said and with `or` it failed although the whole assertion held. Only a first line that did not parse on its own was reported, as a confusing "expected a value at column 16". Separately, `check -p` on a lone test file reported "microflow not found" for a target a setup script creates, with no sign that the script-set form (`check setup.mdl x.test.mdl -p`) resolves it
cause: parseAnnotations read the doc comment one line at a time and expectPattern/verifyPattern captured the rest of the tag's own line; a following ` * …` line carries no tag, so it matched nothing and fell through every branch. The patterns also required text on the tag line (`\s+(.+)`), so a bare `@expect` with the expression below it was dropped whole
fix: @expect and @verify open an annotation whose text runs, as a javadoc block tag's does, to the next `@tag` line or the end of the comment; the joined text (single spaces) is what ParseExpect/ParseVerify compile. Text after the tag that is not part of the expression therefore makes the assertion an ERROR whose message says it spans N lines and that a description goes before the first tag. @test/@setup/@cleanup/@throws stay one line, so prose under a test's name is still description. check prints a hint naming the script-set form under a test file's "not found" reference errors, and check/test --help say a test file can be one of the set
insight: The same silent-absence shape as the original @expect fix (#46), one level up: that fix made a line the parser could not compile an error, but a line the parser never LOOKED at was still dropped. `--list` printing the truncated text back is what made it look wired. Javadoc's rule (a block tag's text continues to the next tag) is the fail-closed choice; stopping at a blank line was considered and rejected because it re-opens the silent drop for an expression with a blank line in it, at the cost of turning prose written after the tags (seen once, in upgrade_source_test's fixture) into an ERROR with a message naming the fix. Runtime A/B on 11.13.0 (`mxcli test --local --db-type hsqldb`): baseline PASSED `$r = 'a;b'` + `and length($r) = 4` and FAILED the true `or` assertion with "expected $r = 'zzz', actual: a;b"; fixed inverts both. The paren-on-line-1 fixture is what makes `make check-mdl` fail if the continuation is lost again. Sibling not fixed: an untagged line after @throws is still ignored, so `@throws` + a message on the next line becomes "any exception"
